title.narrative: EDCTP2: European & Dev. Countries Clinical Trials Partnership 2015 - 2026
EDCTP2: European & Dev. Countries Clinical Trials Partnership 2015 - 2026

description.narrative:
BAKGRUND Partnerskapet mellan Europa och utvecklingsländer inom området klinisk prövning (EDCTP) inrättades 2003 för att hantera den globala hälsokris som orsakas av de tre största fattigdomsrelaterade sjukdomarna hiv/aids, malaria och tuberkulos och för att fullgöra EU:s åtagande att uppnå FN:s millennieutvecklingsmål till 2015. Sverige har genom Sida bidragit med biståndsmedel till EDCTP och Sida har i enlighet med regeringens beslut den 23 oktober 2003 (UD2003/ 53044/ GU) företrätt Sverige inom EDCTP:s första program.
För genomförandet av EDCTP2 har en stiftelse med säte i Haag, Nederländerna, bildats. Medverkande stater ska utse en myndighet/ institution som företrädare och medlem i stiftelsen.
Erfarenheterna av svensk medverkan under partnerskapets första program är mycket goda. Regeringen anser att Sveriges engagemang i EDCTP ska fortsätta under det andra programmet, och har erhållit riksdagens bemyndigande att besluta om deltagande i den stiftelse som inrättats som genomförandestruktur för EDCTP2 (prop. 2014/15:1 utg.omr. 7, bet. 2014/ 15:UU2, rskr. 2014/15:75). Enligt regeringens beslut ska "finansiering av det svenska deltagandet sker genom medel som Sida disponerar inom ramen för utgiftsområde 7, anslag 1:1 Biståndsverksamhet".
Regeringen har beslutat (Regeringsbeslut UF2015/ 12547/UD/USTYR) att Sverige ska delta och har uppdragit åt Sida att företräda Sverige i den stiftelse som bildats som genomförandestruktur (EDCTP2- IS) för det andra programmet för partnerskap mellan Europa och Afrika inom området kliniskprövning (EDCTP2).
Programmet är 10 år, men Sidas beslut handlar enbart om medelstilldelning för kommande femårsperiod av EDCTP2 programmet.
I tillägg till Sidas bidrag ska Sverige räkna in alla offentliga medel som går till forskning inom EDCTP2 fokusområden som del av det totala bidraget. Det inkluderar Sidas bidrag inom globala och bilaterala samarbeten samt Vetenskapsrådets och andra relevanta svenska myndigheters bidrag till forskning inom EDCTP2 fokusområden.
UPPDRAGET EDCTP syftar till att stödja forskningssamarbete som accelererar den kliniska utvecklingen av nya eller förbättrade interventioner för att förebygga eller behandla HIV/AIDS, tuberkulos, malaria och andra försummade infektionssjukdomar i Afrika söder om Sahara.
PROGRAMMET Det andra EDCTP-programmet (EDCTP2) genomförs som en del av det europeiska ramprogrammet för forskning och Innovation, ”Horizon 2020”. Europeiska unionens bidrag till EDCTP kan uppgå till 683 miljoner euro för det 10-åriga programmet (2014-2024), förutsatt att detta motsvaras av bidrag från de deltagande europeiska staterna.
DELTAGANDE De länder som deltar i EDCTP2 som medlemmar i föreningen EDCTP i oktober 2015 är: 14 europeiska länder-Österrike, Danmark, Finland, Frankrike, Tyskland, Irland, Italien, Luxemburg, Nederländerna, Norge, Portugal, Spanien, Sverige, UK; och 14 afrikanska länder – Burkina Faso, Kamerun, Kongo, Gabon, Gambia, Ghana, Mali, Moçambique, Niger, Senegal, Sydafrika, Tanzania, Uganda och Zambia. Flera länder kan komma att ansluta.
STYRELSEFORMER EDCTP stiftelsen kommer att genomföra EDCTP2-programmet. Stiftelsen styrs av sina medlemmar, de deltagande europeiska och afrikanska staterna, genom generalförsamlingen. Sekretariatet utför verksamheten inom programmet. Det främsta vetenskaplig rådgivande organ till generalförsamlingen och sekretariatet är den rådgivande vetenskaplig kommitté (Scientific Advisory Committee).

Support to European and Developing Countries Clinical Trials Partnership to accelerate development of new or improved druugs , vaccines, microbicides and diagnostics against HIV/AIDS; TB and malaria. Support provided since 2004. A new expanded programme is planned within Horizon2020 which will be called EDCTP2.
To accelerate research and development of new or improved diagnostics, drugs, microbicides and vaccines against HIV/AIDS, tuberculosis, malaria and NIDs.

description.narrative:
The EDCTP2 programme is in its completion phase, no new annual work plan or new calls have been published and the EDCTP Secretariat has focused on reviewing periodic and final reports, tracking the progress of projects, collecting outputs, and managing project closures.
As previously reported, the EDCTP2 programme was planned to run until the end of 2024, but due to the COVID-19 pandemic, the end of the programme has been extended until the end of 2026 to allow completion of all project grants (no-cost extensions of project duration). Likewise, Sida has extended the end date of the activity period of the agreement with the EDCTP Association until the end of 2026.
Examples of project results
The EDCTP2 programme has adhered to its strategic vision and continues to deliver significant impact on poverty-related diseases and clinical research capacity in sub-Saharan Africa. Out of 48 projects supported by Sida, 33 were closed and 14 had reached their end date with final payments and reporting pending in the end of 2025. One project was still ongoing with an expected end date in March 2026.
Research area: Vaccine and neutralising antibody development for disease prevention
Prevention of diarrhoeal disease in children:
Diarrhoeal diseases continue to pose a serious threat to children in low- and middle-income countries. A leading cause of diarrhoea is enterotoxigenic E. coli (ETEC), a gut bacterium that can quickly lead to dehydration and require hospitalisation. Beyond the immediate dehydration risk, repeated bouts of diarrhoea can slow childrens growth, hinder learning, and limit future opportunities.
Sida is contributing to two projects on a vaccine (ETVAX) developed by the Swedish biopharma company Scandinavian Biopharma Holding AB against diarrheal disease caused by ETEC. A phase IIb clinical trial in infants aged 6 to 18 months in The Gambia demonstrated that ETVAX is safe and immunogenic and offers protection against ETEC, when considering all co-infections. A reduction of all-cause moderate-to-severe diarrhoea was observed, suggesting a broader public health benefit. The results of the study were published in The Lancet Infectious Diseases (doi: 10.1016/S1473-3099(25)00774-1) and the European Medicines Agency reviewed the trials data and agreed that the vaccine candidate is ready to move forward to a pivotal phase III clinical trial. The consortium is currently seeking funding to carry out the phase III trial.
Research area: Drugs for treatment and prevention
Malaria treatment:
The Sida-supported PAMAfrica consortium is conducting clinical trials to develop next-generation malaria treatments for Africa. There is currently no evidence-based treatment for babies weighing less than 5 kg with malaria. In April 2024, the PAMAfrica consortium announced positive results from their phase II/III CALINA study demonstrating that a new dose regimen of an existing treatment has good efficacy and safety for the smallest babies with malaria. The treatment called Coartem Baby was granted authorisation by the Swiss Agency for Therapeutic Products under the Marketing Authorisation for Global Health Products procedure in July 2025, and received World Health Organization (WHO) prequalification in April 2026. WHO prequalification ensures that the treatment meets international standards of quality, safety and efficacy and will enable global health procurers to include the treatment in their programmes and facilitate broader access to this vulnerable population. Coartem Baby is the first and only antimalarial developed specifically for newborns and young infants weighing from 2 to 5 kg and the prequalification of the treatment marks a major milestone in closing a long-standing treatment gap affecting some 30 million babies born each year in malaria-endemic areas of Africa.
In addition to the clinical study work, the PAMAfrica consortium has contributed to research capacity strengthening and training in a number of relevant areas including good clinical practice, health research ethics, scientific writing and communication skills.
Publications
In the end of 2025, the EDCTP Secretariat recorded more than 500 scientific publications associated with Sida-funded projects (out of more than 2500 publications from all projects under the EDCTP2 programme). The majority of publications are related to projects in the emerging diseases area (56%), highlighting Sida's substantial contributions to research in this area, followed by HIV and HIV-associated infections (17%), malaria (10%), capacity building and training (6%), tuberculosis (4,5%), diarrhoeal diseases (3%), neglected infectious diseases (3%) and lower respiratory tract infections (0,5%).
Clinical research
Sida funds have supported 86 clinical studies being conducted on EDCTP projects of which 59% were clinical trials and interventional studies, i.e. studies of drugs, vaccines and broadly neutralising antibodies as well as diagnostics trials. The remaining studies were observational studies including cohort and epidemiological studies. Of the clinical trials, the majority evaluated the safety and efficacy of new of improved medical interventions (phase II/III trials) reflecting the intention set out in the EDCTP Strategic Business Plan to support the most critical phases of clinical development.
Importantly, the EDCTP2 programme has succeeded in focusing on studies involving populations that are often excluded from clinical research but that have major unmet medical needs. 54% of the clinical studies supported by Sida involved populations with unmet medical needs including pregnant and lactating women and their children, newborns and infants, children as well as adolescents.
Individual research capacity strengthening
Sida-funding has provided training opportunities for 221 sub-Saharan African researchers (47% female, 53% male) at Bachelor, Master, PhD and postdoctoral level. 67% of the trainees are undertaking their training at an institution in sub-Saharan Africa.
